title: Adic completions respect ring equivalences
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings, I and J ideals, and e : R \simeq S a ring equivalence with J = e(I). Their adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] admit a ring equivalence E commuting with the canonical maps: E composed with R to its completion equals e followed by S to its completion.

source.place: Definition 07GH and Proposition 07PV, quotient presentation; inverse-limit construction from algebra.tex Section 00M9

proof.text: Ideal.quotientEquiv for each power gives the bijectivity of the quotient maps induced by e.
Apply RingTheory.pair_henselization_completion_data to e. Its inverse compatibility implies the required forward compatibility by injectivity of the inverse completion equivalence.

mathlib_searches.query: adic completion is invariant under ring isomorphism
A ring equivalence mapping an ideal to another induces compatible ring equivalence of adic completions
mathlib_searches.results: AdicCompletion.congr is for linear equivalences with fixed scalar ring; ofAlgEquiv requires completeness. Neither is the stated compatible ring equivalence.

mathlib_searches.query: AdicCompletion.*[Ee]quiv in Mathlib and both library roots
mathlib_searches.results: No exact transport theorem. quotientEquiv, liftRingHom, eval and ext_eval are used.

lean.statement:
theorem AdicCompletion.exists_ringEquiv
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (I : Ideal R) (J : Ideal S) (e : R ≃+* S) (h : J = I.map e) :
    ∃ E : AdicCompletion I R ≃+* AdicCompletion J S,
      E.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion I R)) =
        (algebraMap S (AdicCompletion J S)).comp e.toRingHom
